UNNC FoSE Success at ICOIE 2023
14 July 2023
The 2023 International Conference on Open and Innovative Education (ICOIE 2023) was held in Hong Kong Metropolitan University (HKMU) 4-6 July. This was the 10th conference in the series, and the first time to have it in person since the COVID pandemic.
UNNC had six papers accepted at ICOIE this year, five of which had authors from the Faculty of Science and Engineering (FoSE). Five UNNC colleagues attended in person (four from FoSE), and a couple of others presented online. Three of the FoSE papers included students as co-authors, which is in line with some of the previous FoSE ICOIE papers. This year, the FoSE paper by Boon Giin Lee, Matt Pike, Joseph Thenara (class of 2023) and Dave Towey ("Fighting Fires with Mixed Reality: The Future of Fire Safety Training and Education") won an Excellent Paper award.
FoSE has an excellent track record with ICOIE, including several Best/Excellent paper awards, and a large number of proceedings papers being invited to (and eventually published in) high-quality journals.
As a key element of some of the FoSE papers, collaboration with our undergraduate students in curricular and extra-curricular research --- including our
Faculty Undergraduate Research Projects
--- has been a very important part of the success of the papers and presentations (and, of course, the underlying projects and research). As one of the lead authors on a joint staff-student paper said: "Collaborating on papers with undergraduate students, despite the challenges posed by their limited experience in crafting writing styles, has been a truly enjoyable experience for me. I greatly admire their enthusiasm and dedication, and I look forward to engaging in further and deeper collaborations with ambitious and motivated students in the future."
Some comments from the FoSE team at ICOIE this year were:
"For me, the ICOIE conference serves as an excellent platform for sharing my research with peers from around the world. It also provides a great opportunity for networking and keynotes from the leaders in the field of educational technology. It has been a prosperous and rewarding experience participating in this years ICOIE conference."
"Attending ICOIE this year was an amazing experience. It marked the first time I presented my research in person since the pandemic began. I had the opportunity to meet new people, showcase my research, and hold productive meetings with my collaborators in Hong Kong. Overall, it was a truly memorable event."
"It has been another excellent ICOIE. It was great to meet many of the ICOIE community in person again, for the first time since COVID. The keynotes, panels, and parallel sessions offered a lot of interesting ideas; and the in-person discussions will surely lead to new collaborations and projects. UNNC/FoSE were again very high profile, and our presentations attracted a lot of good questions and suggestions. We're looking forward to ICOIE 2024."
The authors gratefully acknowledge the support provided by FoSE through the FoSE T&L Conference Research grants.

title: Ningbo Digital Humanities Lab showcase at the 2023 Maritime Silk Road Culture and Tourism Expo
content:
The goal of this expo is to promote exchanges and mutual learning with cities along the Maritime Silk Road on the occasion of the 10th anniversary of the Belt and Road Initiative, facilitate win-win cooperation in the domestic and international cultural and tourism industries, demonstrate the new achievements of Zhejiang's innovative culture and cultural innovation, and promote the integrated development of production, city, and culture in Ningbo Port. With this objective in mind, seven participating units, including Ningbo Marine Research Institute, Ningbo University of Technology, University of Nottingham Ningbo China, Zhejiang University Software College, Ningbo VisionRDI Optoelectronics Co., Ltd., and Baolue Technology (Zhejiang) Co., Ltd., showcased more than 60 exhibits, focusing on the integration of digital technology and cultural tourism industries, creating a creative exhibition space that combines technology, interest, and interactivity, and providing the audience with a peak and cutting-edge cultural and technological industry experience, fully demonstrating the infinite charm of "Culture + Technology."
The UNNC Digital Humanities Lab is a large interdisciplinary research laboratory dedicated to the thematic research of Ningbo's history. It aims to deeply explore, document, preserve, and present the historical development of Ningbo city using digital humanities technologies, reconstruct historical Ningbo, and create a resource-rich, authoritative, and comprehensive public open platform. The research content covers local history and culture, climate, literature, religion, historical maps, historical photographs, urban morphology, water resources management, urban landscapes, and more. Dr Jing Xie, an associate professor in Architecture and Urban Design, Dr Yu-Ting Tang, an associate professor in Environmental Sciences, and Dr Tengwen Long, an assistant professor in Environmental Sciences, have made outstanding research achievements in this field.

ABE Talks Urban Innovation Lab: Recombinant Urbanism 2023
Recombinant Urbanism 2023; 4 Urban Design Models and the Asian Megacity/Metacity acceleration (with some student case studies).
Speaker:
Professor DAVID GRAHAME SHANE Columbia GSAPP
Date:
Wednesday 17
th
May 2023
Venue:
IEB 122 19:30-20:30
Abstract:
This lecture will briefly outline the paradigm shift faced by urban designers as a result of the the earlier three urban models used in the development of cities in the Anthropocene age and their climate impacts. Kevin Lynch (1981) described these models as The City of Faith (imperial model), the City Machine (industrial model) and the emerging EcoCity. The lecture adds the Fragmented Metropolis model as a transition to the megacity/metacity of information now emerging, perhaps forming the Ecocity. It will examine the current fragmented model of the metropolis and the implications of the emerging megacity/ metacity of information for future cities. Designers have always operated between desired utopias and feared dystopias, creating fragile balances in models to ensure survival. The question now is how to set the balance for the next century. The lecture will end with some case studies of current dynamic urban growth in Asian cities (Tokyo, Shenzhen, Chandigarh) and study reworking older urban systems in Europe (Barcelona) and Latin America (San Juan PR).
About the Speaker:
David Grahame Shane studied at the Architectural Association, London (AA Dipl 1969), and at Cornell for an M.Arch (Urban Design 1972) and an Architectural and Urban History PhD (1978) with Professors Colin Rowe and Chris Otto.
He taught at the AA in the 1970’s for Alvin Boyarsky and at Bennington College, before starting at Columbia in the 1980’s, in UD since 1991. He has lectured widely and published in Europe, USA and Asia.
He is the author of
Recombinant Urbanism: Conceptual Modeling in Architecture, Urban Design and City Theory
(2005) and
Urban Design Since 1945; a Global Perspective
(2011) and co-edited “Sensing the 21st Century City: Close-Up and Remote
” (Architectural Design
2005). His article “Gardens as Public Space; A Century of Continuity and Change in the Great Bay Area” is in
The Emerging Public Realm of the Great Bay Area
(2021 Taylor and Francis). His “Notes Towards an Intellectual Biography of Colin Rowe 1938-78” will appear in the forthcoming
The Urban Design Legacy of Colin Rowe (
ORO Editions
).
He is currently editing the
Archigram Oral Archives
for m+ museum HK.

Abstract:
These
notes
record and expand the lectures for the “Journées Equations aux Dérivées Partielles 2018” held during the week of June 11-15, 2018. The aim is to give an overview of the classical theory for the obstacle problem, and then present some recent developments on the regularity of the free boundary.
Biography:
Alessio Figalli is an Italian mathematician working at ETH Zurich who received the Fields Medal at the International Congress of Mathematicians (ICM) in 2018.
In 2006, he graduated from the Scuola Normale Superiore of Pisa (SNS) and the University of Pisa where his dissertation on optimal transportation on non-compact manifolds was supervised by Luigi Ambrosio, who is now Director of the SNS. From his first year in 2002, Alessio surprised students and staff of the school with his vivid interest in mathematics and his ability to attend and understand first year modules as well as more advanced lectures which were intended for later years’ undergraduate or PhD students. In 2006, word spread of a student applying for the PhD programme with already two papers submitted for publication, an extremely rare achievement for an undergraduate student of Mathematics.
In October 2007, Alessio obtained a PhD from both the Scuola Normale of Pisa and the École Normale Supérieure of Lyon under the joint supervision of Luigi Ambrosio and Cedric Villani with
Optimal Transportation and action-minimizing measures
being the title of his thesis. Alessio spent two years in France, first as a researcher of the European research centre CNRS, and then as Professor at the École Polytechnique. In 2009, he moved from Europe to the United States of America, seizing the opportunity of working with Luis Caffarelli at the University of Texas in Austin (UTA). In the next seven years, Alessio did not just reach the highest professor rank at UTA, but also his paper titled
A mass transportation approach to quantitative isoperimetric inequalities
(with Aldo Pratelli and Francesco Maggi) appeared in 2011 in the prestigious journal
Inventiones Mathematicae
. In 2016, Figalli moved back to Europe where he took up the position of Chaired Professor at ETH Zurich, before being appointed in 2019 as Director of the
Forschungsinstitut für Mathematik
(Institute for Mathematical Research -
FIM
).
The research interests of Alessio Figalli include calculus of variations and partial differential equations (PDEs), with particular emphasis on optimal transportation, Monge-Ampère equations, functional and geometric inequalities, elliptic PDEs of local and non-local type, free boundary problems, Hamilton-Jacobi equations, transport equations with rough vector-fields, and random matrix theory. Up to now, he has published 164 research papers, written with more than fifty research collaborators, and his number of citations exceeds 3000.
During his career Alessio Figalli has received many awards, including the notable European Mathematical Society (EMS) Prize in 2012, and the Stampacchia Gold Medal in 2015. In the ICM of Rio de Janeiro in 2018, he received the Fields Medal, the most important prize in Mathematics, which is often compared to the Nobel Prize. The Fields medal is awarded only once every four years, and Alessio Figalli is the second Italian awardee, 44 years after Enrico Bombieri.
Alessio Figalli has received other honours and titles including the
Knighthood of the Order of Merit of the Italian Republic
which was awarded directly from the President of Italy. Moreover:
One of the asteroids orbiting the Sun (438253) has been named after Alessio Figalli.
In November 2019, the character of Phil Gallis, a mathematician who helps Uncle Scrooge and Donald Duck in the riddle of the
Four Dimensional Corkscrew
in
Topolino (Mickey Mouse),
was based on Alessio Figalli.

Zhejiang Education Department has recently updated their guidance on COVID-19 Epidemic Control over the summer vacation period for all universities and schools in Zhejiang.

title: Update on a cluster of COVID-19 in Beijing
content:
Update on a cluster of COVID-19 in Beijing
15 June 2020
Important advice from Zhejiang and Ningbo authorities regarding the new development of COVID-19 in Beijing.
As many of you will be aware from news articles over the weekend, there have been a number of COVID-19 cases detected in Beijing. Whilst the Beijing authorities are taking the necessary steps to control and manage the situation, we have received notification from the Zhejiang and Ningbo authorities on steps we should take on our epidemic control measures. With immediate effect:
Business trips to Beijing for all UNNC staff and students are suspended;
Staff and students should, where possible, avoid personal trips to Beijing;
Students returning from Beijing to campus are required to contact their Student Support Advisors in advance. The University will make all necessary arrangements for the students before entering campus;
Any member of staff who travelled to Beijing after 30 May are to report this to their Faculty Office and HR; students are to notify their Student Support Advisors.
These arrangements will be updated as the government regulations changes.
Many thanks for your understanding and cooperation.
Security and Safety Office

title: Letter from President Yang  to UNNC returning students
content:
Letter from President Yang to UNNC returning students
24 April 2020
Dear students,
Yesterday, the University announced the schedule for the re-opening of campus. Next week, you'll be back among our familiar, yet too long empty, classrooms and be enjoying the spring sunshine on our green and open spaces.
2020 has so far been a difficult year, to say the very least. Due to the impact of the COVID-19 epidemic, our spring semester started on the internet, and each of us has experienced significant changes in our personal, academic or professional lives. In the face of these challenges, we persevered and came together to finally bring about this long-for reunion.
I would like to thank everyone at the University of Nottingham Ningbo China, who helped each other and fought against the epidemic.
The UNNC Working Group of COVID-19 Prevention and Control has been active since the Chinese New Year's Eve, responding promptly to all kinds of emergencies to ensure the health and safety of our students and staff as well as the orderly introduction of online teaching.
Our administrative staff returned early to work, followed by our academic staff and students. The logistics staff worked round the clock to ensure safety and to bring daily supplies for staff and students remaining on campus.
Our academic staff put all their energy and time into online teaching. I understand that some instructors even set up a special group chat in order to hold effective online sessions. They also used their professional skills to help fight the virus and shared their insights in various fields such as the economy, tourism and the recovery of Ningbo.
To our students, I say that you overcame many difficulties to study at home and cooperated with various epidemic prevention protocols to support the University during this difficult time. You took action proactively and voluntarily collected epidemic prevention equipment to help the broader Nottingham community. Many of you passed on warmth and hope via the internet through music and art.
This epidemic is undoubtedly a disaster, but it also teaches us a number of unique lessons - how to continue studying and learning in such unprecedented circumstances is undoubtedly one of them.
When the University began online teaching, you started to practice independent learning, self-management and self-discipline. These are core qualities that the University is committed to cultivating and one of the competitive advantages of UNNC students. I believe that those adept at autonomous learning will achieve rapid growth while balancing study and daily life.
During social isolation, you are developing your abilities of introspection and critical thinking. Can you calm your anxieties and re-examine the world and yourself? Learning is not limited to universities. What is the nature of the world? What is the destiny of humankind? What is the meaning of life? What attitude should you take when facing a crisis, and what kind of person will you become in the future? Have you ever considered such questions?
Prestigious institutions, libraries, museums and publishers around the globe have opened up their resources and e-commerce is flourishing unprecedentedly, taking the responsibility of supporting people's livelihoods. Remote diagnosis and treatment show the power of technology.
Staying at home should not narrow your vision or limit your ambitions. The impact of the epidemic will be far-reaching and, when it is all over, our world may be very different.
Be diligent in thought and courageous in deed, and be proud of how you reacted during this time. I hope that you can find new ways of thinking, learning and cooperation from this experience to make yourself stronger and make the world better.
No previous generation understands the meaning of globalisation and the concept of “a community of shared destiny” better than yours. The shaping of the new international pattern requires you, UNNC students and prospective international citizens, to stand out and contribute your knowledge, insight and courage.
The University is ready for your return, and we will soon meet again on our beautiful campus. Please be grateful for the seemingly ordinary opportunity to study in the lecture rooms with your peers; please cherish what you possess now and the beauty of the world.
However, the impact of the COVID-19 epidemic is not yet over, and you will still notice certain restrictions upon your campus life. We still need to persist in our efforts and face new challenges together.
I wish you good health, a positive attitude and abundant skills. I hope you can head anywhere in the world with knowledge and empathy and pursue your dreams.
With best wishes
Professor Yang Fujia
President of University of Nottingham Ningbo China

title: UNNC Epidemic Prevention and Control Procedures
content:
UNNC Epidemic Prevention and Control Procedures
23 April 2020
The health and safety of our students and staff is our overriding priority. UNNC is strictly following the full health and safety procedures from local authorities to ensure the smooth recommencement of face-to-face teaching on campus.
Please take note of the regulations of the local authorities as well as those of the University. These regulations aim to ensure the efficient delivery of epidemic prevention and control on campus and lead to a sound environment for your return.
Before students return
A requirement for universities to reopen is that we have to be able to report on the daily health status of our students. To achieve this, we have developed a
WeChat mini programme
which you have seen the details already. Students should cooperate with the University and Student Support Advisors (SSAs) to update accurate information via the WeChat mini programme. Once all requirements are met, students should strictly comply with the arrangements of the University when returning to the campus. An early or delayed return is not advised.
Students should provide daily health updates via the WeChat mini programme, and in the case of any developed symptoms such as fever (>37.3°C), fatigue, dry cough, difficulty breathing or other discomforts, should suspend their return to campus and seek medical treatment.
Students should complete the student return registration via the WeChat mini programme to provide their full travel arrangements.
Students should bring clinical thermometers along with sufficient masks, tissues, alcohol-disinfectant wipes or water-free hand sanitizers and freshness protection packages (for mask disposal).
While travelling
Wear masks correctly when returning to the University, and travel as little as possible by public transportation. Keep hands clean, reduce or avoid touching public facilities and try to avoid touching your mouth, eyes and nose.
Keep your travel documents, such as train or flight tickets, for necessary checks from customs and Centres for Disease Control and Prevention.
We are following the test and isolation regulations from the local health authorities. So students returning from key areas affected by COVID-19 should cooperate with the local health department and take nucleic acid and serum tests and medical observation once arriving in Ningbo. The latest requirement is that students from Hubei, Heilongjiang and Guangdong are required to take nucleic acid and serum tests. Students from Hubei will undertake a 14-day self-isolation in LA hotel.
Campus access
The Campus will be open to the first group of returning students from 8 AM on 26 April.
External visitors without prior approval from the University are not allowed to enter campus during the period of epidemic prevention and control. Parents, other relatives and private cars (unregistered) cannot enter the campus. Students should show campus cards (or ID cards) and a green health code as well as undergo a temperature check to enter the University.
Students are not allowed to leave campus during the period of epidemic prevention and control except for essential purposes such as medical treatment. Students must gain approval from SSAs to leave campus and should return by a specified time. Under no circumstances should students remain off-campus overnight.
Daily health inspection
Student should check their body temperature and health conditions twice a day and report via the WeChat mini programme. Report to UNNC Clinic (dial 88180120) and Student Support Advisors immediately in case you or people nearby show symptoms such as fever, fatigue, dry cough and breathing difficulties. People with fever should wear masks as soon as possible.
Health and safety protocols
Keep hands clean all times. Wash hands before and after meals, after using the toilet and after sneezing or coughing.
Keep dormitories clean and tidy. Daily ventilation is recommended (at least twice a day for more than 30 minutes). Do not visit or gather in other dormitories.
Animals are not allowed inside the student halls of residence. Avoid all contact with wild/stray animals.
Please walk up the stairs if you live on or below the 5th floor. Wear a mask when taking an elevator and wash hands after touching the elevator button.
Reduce unessential travel and do not participate in any large-scale activities or gatherings.
Eating meals in a group is not allowed. Please take food away to eat elsewhere if there are not enough free tables in the canteens.
Please comply with personnel flow restriction regulations in public areas on campus (e.g. library, sports centre) during the epidemic prevention and control period and maintain a social distance within these areas.
Please wear masks in crowded or poorly-ventilated areas such as classrooms, library, and stores in the living area.
Please wear masks while speaking at a close distance or having close contact with others.
Please wear masks when entering the Clinic, observation rooms, and temperature measuring points.
Student affairs management
Please take part in online assemblies delivered by Student Support Advisors and pay close attention to important notices and tips for your return.
The Free Talk service is available and prioritised for students from key areas affected by the epidemic.
Please keep your mobile phones on and your University email box accessible in case of important messages.
Student activities that physically take place on campus are suspended during the period of epidemic prevention and control.
It is highly appreciated that all returning students comply with the University’s epidemic prevention and control protocols. Any violators will likely face disciplinary action.
Please continue to check your email for more information.

title: University of Nottingham cross-campus cooperation against pandemic
content:
University of Nottingham cross-campus cooperation against pandemic
10 April 2020
The infrared radiation thermometers donated by the University of Nottingham (UoN) arrived at Ningbo No.1 Hospital in March. The donations were made possible thanks to funds raised by staff and alumni in both the UK and China.
As the UK is currently facing a challenging situation fighting the COVID-19 epidemic, Ningbo No.1 Hospital has entrusted UNNC to coordinate the donation of masks to UoN's affiliated hospital.
Such mutual help is not limited to medical supplies. On 16th March, Nottingham China Health Institute (NCHI) and UoN Asian Business Centre China jointly held a video conference between the Ningbo No.1 Hospital, the Ningbo medical team in Wuhan and the University of Nottingham UK's affiliated hospital.
During the conference, the teams shared practical experiences of epidemic control and treatment and discussed prospective cooperation in the future. UoN and Ningbo No.1 Hospital will co-establish a long-term distant diagnosis mechanism. Dr Chengbo Wang, an MRI expert at UNNC, agreed to participate in the joint UK-China COVID-19 treatment group and provide advice in the area of medical imaging.
Professor Richard Hubbard, Director of NCHI, commented: "The information from China/Ningbo has been invaluable. The CT images sent from China have become the main teaching document for all of the radiology and respiratory departments. This has been gold dust for us to get ahead of this wave."
Collaboration between Nottingham and Ningbo in public health has a long history. The establishment of NCHI in 2018 brought together international researchers to collaborate with health sector partners, universities and industry to find solutions that meet the required health needs of China's population, aiming to drive improvements in the quality, effectiveness and efficiency of healthcare throughout China.
In the face of the common crisis caused by the spread of Covid-19 coronavirus, the international community needs solidarity and cooperation more than ever before. Over the past few months, UNNC has played an essential role as a bridge between China and the UK, as part of the broader international "Nottingham" community.

title: University rehearses return of students to campus
content:
University rehearses return of students to campus
08 April 2020
8th April: The University held a health and safety drill ahead of the expected return of students to campus.
The drill kicked off at 10 am, with students bused into campus for registration and temperature measurement.
At 10:30 am, the Clinic received a call from a student reporting a fever, cough and fatigue. Within 10 minutes, a clinic staff member arrived at Building 23 carrying medical supplies and wearing a protective outfit.
The clinic staff member instructed the student to wear a surgical mask, transferred him to the nearest isolation room, took his body temperature and asked about his medical history.
After confirming the student’s fever, the clinic staff member reported the information to the fever patient management system of the local health department, and he was transferred to a fever clinic in a special purpose vehicle.
At the same time, security guards and hall receptionists sealed off the student's room while Student Support Advisors guided his roommates to take the campus tour car to the LA Hotel for temporary isolation and to wait for his medical check result.
At 11 am, another group of students entered the campus - however, a thermo-detector alarm indicated that one student had an above-normal temperature.
Security guards notified the standby clinic staff, who immediately transferred the student to the nearest isolation stall and completed all required processes.
Liam, an international student who remained on campus during the winter break, also participated in the drill. "I think the drill was very well thought out and educational," he said. "It thought about many possible situations and provided multiple solutions for each one. I believe that it can help people to be more at ease about coming back."
The University hopes the drill will further enhance its epidemic prevention and control, as well as contribute to campus preparations for returning students. The UNNC working group of COVID-19 prevention and control continue to draw up plans for the return of student to UNNC.
The University has implemented the regular disinfection of the campus, ensured that there are enough epidemic prevention supplies, established a joint prevention and control mechanism with local health institutions and formulated a canteen management and food safety guarantee system. In addition, UNNC will carry out further self-examination and improvement as regulated by Zhejiang Province to ensure the health of returning staff and students.

title: Update to all students and staff
content:
Update to all students and staff
03 April 2020
At today’s press conference held by Zhejiang Provincial Government, in addition to providing an update on the latest COVID-19 prevention and control situation, they also provided an update on the timetable for education establishments to re-open in the province. The timetable is:
• The final year of high schools and the final year of middle schools will re-open on 13 April. The remainder of the grades in these schools, along with primary school grades four to six will re-open after 20 April.
• Primary school grades one to three will re-open after 26 April.
• Kindergartens are expected to re-open after 6 May.
• Universities have been instructed to prepare for re-opening in late April, with specific dates to be announced in due course.
As already communicated, our detailed planning for students to return to UNNC was submitted to the local Education Bureau in early March and we continue to keep in contact with them. As soon as we receive official notification of our re-opening date, we will let you know and also publish the sequenced student return plan on our website.
The press conference also stated that international students and international staff currently overseas are, temporarily, not to return to China. As UNNC communicated previously, the Chinese Government decided to temporarily suspend the entry into China of foreign nationals holding visas or residence permits.
On a related note, as Monday 6 April is a public holiday, we will delay our regular Monday message to Wednesday 8 April. Please continue to check the University website, wechat and emails for further updates.
Many thanks for your cooperation.

title: Chinese Culture Heritage Event: Sweet Dumplings Making
content:
10 Feb, about 50 staff gathered around at MN canteen to celebrate the Lantern Festival by making sweet dumplings and playing the lantern riddles game. The celebration began with a video introducing the custom of Lantern Festival. Professor Khong, Dean of NUBS China, welcomed all the participants and wished everyone a very happy and successful new year.
It was said that Ningbo was the originate place of sweet dumplings – Tangyuan. The tradition of eating Tangyuan in Ningbo could date back to Song Dynasty. Mixing sticky rice flour and water, putting sesame and lard oil inside a piece of paste, kneading it to round shape, and cooking in boiled water. The sweet dumping is ready to taste. The small white rice ball brought great fun to the participants.
Simultaneously, the participants also played another traditional game – lantern riddles. As the zodiac of this year is rabbit, participants who got the right answer of the lantern riddle received a rabbit key ring for gift.
This event was jointly organized by Confucius Institute and HR Department.

title: Chinese Language Partner Activity Received Warm Welcome
content:
19 Oct, the first Chinese language partner activity was held at TB107. Over 20 pairs of language partners engaged in on that day. Different from the traditional talking-oriented activity, this one encouraged the participants to accomplish a task together. During the process, they would talk more, learn more and remember more. Painting masks of Peking Opera and making Chinese knots together during the first activity created a lot of topics amongst the language partners. 2 hours’ activity seemed fairly short.
Aimed to help the Mandarin learners to ‘learn with fun’, CI had made plan for this program for long. With the support from excellent student representatives from the Mandarin Corner society, this activity was eventually put into effect. The activity would regularly practice on 3-5pm every Wednesday afternoon. The natural and real communication environment was expected to bring the Mandarin learners a different experience.
Non-native Chinese speakers who would like to join the event, please feel free to contact
Zhiwei.ge@nottingham.edu.cn
Schedule for the following weeks
3.00- 5.00pm 24 Oct TB109 Chess game
3.00- 5.00pm 31 Oct TBC Chinese food
3.00- 5.00pm 14 Nov TB109 Poem and literature
3.00- 5.00pm 21 Nov TB109 Paper cut
3.00- 5.00pm 28 Nov TB109 Sports
3.00- 5.00pm 5 Dec TB109 Film
3.00- 5.00pm 12 Dec TB109 Calligraphy
Special thanks to Mandarin Corner Society and volunteer Chinese speaking partners.

title: Chinese painting class began
content: 14 Oct, at TB119 the first Chinese painting class for this semester began. 32 students, staff and staff family participated in the class. Same as the past semesters, this class was still delivered by Mr Qingyu Li. Based on his understanding about the UNNC students, staff and staff family’s preference and skills, Mr Li prepared the traditional Chinese realistic painting – lotus – as the topic of the first class. In the following sessions, more complicated skills and different themes would be presented. Special thanks to volunteers from UNNC Chinese Painting and Calligraphy society, who made this class feasible to all the participants.

title: Celebrating Mid-Autumn Festival
content:
7 Sep 2022 at MN Canteen, over 70 staff and their family members engaged in the Mid-Autumn Festival celebrating the event. This event is jointly organized by Confucius Institute and Department of Human Resources. According to the Chinese tradition, the Mid-Autumn Festival is a day for the reunion of the family members. On this occasion, the university leader Chief Financial and Planning Officer Thomas Murphy delivered a speech to welcome all the new staff and existing staff to reunite at UNNC.
Then the participants watched a video to learn the custom about the Mid-Autumn Festival and a legend of
Chang’e
. They were also interested in the China’s Moon Exploration Project, which is named after the Chang’e story.
Finally, the most interesting part Mooncake DIY started. Some participants commented ‘It is a great event. I would love to attend more events like this.’

个人简介
I am Module Convenor for the Introduction to Information Technology course (ITIT), team leader for Writing Lab@UNNC Y1 and an EAP Tutor. As team leader for Writing Lab Y1, I am responsible for support material, workshops and advising for all first year students. The team won the Lord Dearing Award and the Vice Chancellor's medal in 2019. I was Campus Senior Tutor from 2017 to 2019 and was responsible for university-wide pastoral care provision. I was academic lead for the Student Online Induction program (2017-18). From 2015-2016, I was Preliminary Year Student Support Officer with responsibility for the Personal Tutorial system, the Learning Community Forum, and represented CELE on the Senior Tutor Network. I won two awards to support the use of coaching techniques among struggling students.
I have researched the relationship between attendance, grades and pass rates and presented on this topic at the 2016 Teaching and Learning conference at UNNC and the 2017 InForm conference in Malaysia. I have also researched student adaptation to UNNC and presented on this topic at the 2019 InForm conference in Reading, UK. I have also published on the topic of Students as Change Agents and have a publication pending on the topic of Recognition and Response to Students at Risk of Failure.
In the Centre for English Language Education, I have taught on a range of Preliminary Year, Pre-Master’s and Pre-Sessional courses and was responsible for the development of a module on academic integrity. I was responsible for the development of the Nottingham Reading Scheme, creating a Nottingham Advantage Award for extensive reading, and was able to send four students to international conferences in the UK and Japan.
I have taught English in Sudan, Portugal, China, Japan and the UK. I was the co-ordinator of a team-teaching project in Tokyo for 4 years, and the Director of two British Council Summer Schools. I have also worked as a primary school teacher. Before joining UNNC, I worked for Glasgow University where one of my duties was responsibility for language support for students on the Dumfries Campus.
At undergraduate level, I have taught courses in Linguistics, English Dialects, Sociolinguistics, Cross-Cultural Communication, Phonetics and Phonology, Assessment and Testing along with Language Skills. At the university of Glasgow, I specialized in English for Medical and Biological Sciences, though I have also taught English for Engineers, and English for Business Students. At post-graduate level, I have been partly responsible for the development and teaching of short-term advanced academic writing skills courses.

title: 2021 UNNC International Curriculum Research Learning Class
content:
With the heatwave and the scorching sun, the two-week UNNC International Curriculum Research Learning Class was carried out smoothly with the joint efforts of teachers and students. This programme aims at improving students' English abilities, IELTS skills, and learning skills. The programme had fun lessons and targeted assignments to improve students' English language skills, to help students improve their IELTS and learning ability.
In the afternoon of July 4th, the students entered the campus and settled themselves down to learn. Under the guidance of the teaching assistants, they had a campus tour around the beautiful campus of UNNC.
A welcome dinner buffet was provided at M&N Restaurant. Students enjoyed delicious and nutritious dishes such as including pastries, sushi, pasta, fruit, vegetables, fish, and chicken.
The opening ceremony was held in the International Conference Centre in the first evening. Simon Attwood, the Academic Principal of AHS, began his speech with a vivid story to illustrate the help that a school can provide to students and how students can get the help appropriately and set sail in their future life. Subsequently, the leaders of the Affiliated High School also emphasised the moral education.
On the following day, the UNNC International Curriculum Research Learning Class officially started. Before the course, the teachers evaluated the students' strengths and weaknesses through the placement test, and then conducted personalised teaching, so as to provide targeted guidance in the subsequent courses to help students enhance their strengths and improve the weaknesses.
After intensive online testing, students were divided into three classes for small-class teaching. Small-class teaching can better provide personalised teaching guidance and targeted feedback as well as oral practice simulation and guidance.
During the first week from 5th to 9th July, students would wake up around 7 a.m. every day to have meals in an orderly manner. They start the day with practicing English listening from 8:20 in the morning.
The morning session focuses on IELTS, including speaking, listening, reading, composition, and course summary. It mainly exercises students' English learning skills which are targeted in the four sections of IELTS to improve students' test skills. This aspect of the curriculum is conducive to students to lay a solid foundation for IELTS testing, and to cultivate good English learning habits so that students can adapt to the future learning life more quickly. Students will understand their shortcomings and advantages, and can be more targeted in exercising and systematic learning.
The afternoon sessions focus on learning skills to enrich students' learning strategies and enhance their learning ability. The learning content is rich and interesting, including employability, critical thinking, learning styles, creative learning, intercultural communication, learning motivation, time management, academic writing, and active reading. According to the conversations with the students, the afternoon sessions are very interesting and attractive. The teachers are experienced and good at guiding students. They are very patient in teaching, encouraging students to participate actively.
Accompanied and guided by teachers, the self-study also went very smoothly, which mainly focused on the expansion of vocabulary and consolidation of fundamental knowledge that is learnt so far. Through some interesting games, students increase vocabulary and strengthen memory. Evening self-study sessions are for IELTS learning skills, reading, and content learning skills, and other courses.
The overall content is rewarding and the study is enjoyable. Students are learning while thinking while gaining employability with interesting learning activities. In addition to learning, the summer course also allows students to experience the variety of the life in a British style university, accessing to a different way of learning, and at the same time to develop the ability of independent learning.

title: ITE - Beijing Dongcheng Teacher Training Institute Enhancement project
content:
Beijing Dongcheng Teacher Training Institute Enhancement project in the English Education was successfully held at UNNC from 14th to 18th October.
Elite Teacher Training Programme, as a major programme under the Institute for Teaching Excellence (ITE), had brought together eight experienced tutors from CELE and School of Education and English to deliver a 5-day high quality and diverse course for the 31 teachers from Beijing Dongcheng district.
As the first sino-foreign university in China, UNNC provided trainees with a comprehensive and immersive English learning experience. Trainees discussed various topics in a form of group in a pure English teaching environment, they cooperated and made progress with each other, developing new ideas and methods for English teaching.
This is the second cohort from Beijing Dongcheng Teachers' Training and Research Center that ITE has collaborated with since the ITE’s establishment. In the 5-day training, the dedicated and erudite academic team, in the spirit of striving for excellence, selflessly and seriously solved the problems of the trainees in their teaching. At the same time, the effective cooperation of the teaching and logistics force among the various departments of the university was also demonstrated.

title: From Here to The World - 2019 CRRC Qing'dao Sifang English Fans Club International English Enhancement Project
content:
This course used a combination of language skills and business situations to enable trainees to learn practical English expressions more effectively in a simulated environment. Thus in the future, enterprises can better enhance the overall international competitiveness and create a broader impact by improving the quality of talent. In addition to regular courses such as pronunciations, the tutors have developed systematic training materials and case studies based on the industry characteristics, to help trainees better understand business communication and other communication skills in the English language environment.
The final presentation marked the end of this program. On Thursday midnight, most of the trainees stayed up late in the training room of IAMET and prepared for their presentations. They tried their best to prepare fully for the final assessment and demonstrated what they had learnt in the past week.
Team-building and sports activities were also organised for the trainees, such as an ice-breaking event on Monday evening and fun sports on Wednesday evening. Through these activities, the trainees encouraged themselves to gain more motivation for learning, improved mutual understanding, and harvested happiness and friendship. Additionally, they deeply felt the importance of being a team player and said they would continue to apply such team cohesion to their work in the future.

Biography
Dr. Hong Zhang has been teaching in the Centre for English Language Education (CELE) at the University of Nottingham Ningbo China (UNNC) since 2016 Sept. He is a CELE Content Tutor in Business and Economics, and Mathematics and Statistics for Business and Economics. He teaches courses for CELE PYP undergraduate students from NUBS. As a core member of teaching faculty for CELE PYP international foundation pathway, Hong specializes in developing and teaching mathematics and statistics for business and economics. He has successfully and independently designed and created two foundation pathway courses for CELE PYP: one is ‘Introduction to Mathematics for Business and Economics’ (module code: CELEF010), the other one is ‘Introduction to Statistics for Business and Economics (module code: CELEF009)’. Now, he is also the module convenor for 'Introduction to Business Economics' (CELEN042) as well as CELE International Business Team Leader since 2021.
Dr. Hong Zhang holds a bachelor degree in business management from University of Nottingham, a master degree with the distinction in accounting and finance from University of Durham, and a doctoral degree in finance from Nottingham University. Dr. Hong has a long-term commitment to both teaching and research – oriented HE career. His main research interests lie in corporate finance, corporate governance, financial reporting, Fintech, corporate innovation and so on. His recent research outputs have been published in world-leading journals in finance such as International Journal of Finance and Economics, International Journal of Financial Analysis. One of his academic articles on corporate governance was nominated for the 2018 best paper award by International Corporate Governance Society (ICGS). In the same year, he was awarded the UNNC 2017-18 Top Performer for the contributions to CELE PYP curriculum development as well as influential research outputs.

Biography
Sannia Mareta’s journey with the University of Nottingham Ningbo China (UNNC) was started in 2013 by conducting a research-based doctoral study with the focus on developing the compliant-based actuation mechanism, a novel actuation method for controlling vibration that can be used for various vibration control applications, including for vehicle suspension systems. The work introduces the benefits of using compliant actuators for vibration control over well-established rigid actuators and comprises in-depth analysis on a simulation-based model for the combined compliant actuator and vehicle suspension. During these periods, she has also helped with supervising four final year engineering students and an overseas intern working on programming and actuator-related projects. In 2014-2015, she participated in the International Doctoral Innovation Centre (IDIC) PhD Innovation Competition, developing a multifunctional device for human alertness in a form of “smart glove”, which led the team to winning the 2nd prize. The glove aimed to prevent accidents caused by drunk-driving or sleep-deprived problems and to improve efficiency for industrial workers. This achievement has been well publicised by a number of printed and online media in Ningbo and Zhejiang Province, such as shown through the two links below.- http://nb.zjol.com.cn/system/2014/09/29/020282829.shtml- http://hzdaily.hangzhou.com.cn/dskb/html/2014-10/08/content_1812902.htm
In the following year, she then received a prestigious “Dream Scholarship” award from Professor Yang Fujia, the President of the University of Nottingham, for her dedication towards science and technology innovation to the university. Back in 2012 during her undergraduate study, her team’s work on “superhero stove” has also been awarded the 1st prize in the National Innovative Ergonomics Product Design Competition, Indonesia. The proposed stove consisted of intelligent sensing and control systems associated with energy efficient principle, bridging the needs of safety and security values during cooking whilst one has to multitask with other daily activities.
In November 2017, Dr Sannia Mareta joined CELE as a Preliminary Year Science Tutor and now is appointed as the Science and Engineering Academic Content Team Leader. She is also currently leading a university-wide project named V-ROOM, which focuses on research, development, and utilisation of virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), and mixed reality (MR) technologies, funded by Ningbo Education Bureau. This project primarily aims at developing virtual contents to enhance students' learning experience through digitalised and immersive teaching and learning environment; it is now thriving towards various interdisciplinary applications.

Biography
As one of the first graduates of the University of Nottingham Ningbo (UNNC), Dr. Yiben Ma completed his undergraduate degree here in 2008. Before joining The Centre for English Language Education (CELE) as a Preliminary Year Tutor in International Communication, he was a teaching fellow in UNNC’s School of International Communications where he taught various modules on media and communication. He obtained an MA from King’s College London and a PhD from the University of Leeds.
His research mainly focuses on Chinese nationalism and the role of the internet in shaping nationalist politics in contemporary China. Specifically, he is interested in the specificity, structure and power relations of Chinese nationalism in the context of online communication. In addition, he also has keen research interests in political communication in China, including but not limited to critical discourse analysis of political texts, propaganda, media and social changes.

title: 申请须知
content:
申请者请提交完整的研究生申请表、一份研究计划书,两份推荐信(学术方面)、一份成绩单以及英语测试成绩(英语为非母语者)。
在提交正式申请前,可参考商学院博士生导师名单以及他们的研究方向,从而发现和自己研究兴趣一致的教授。
博士录取主要取决于学术能力以及是否有合适的导师两方面。在这一过程中,研究提案的质量至关重要,其将决定能否为学生找到合适的导师,从而最终决定学生能否被录取。
学生被录取到商学院后通常直接攻读博士学位,但是,每年都需要通过年度考核,从而保持其博士研究生资格,否则将可能被降级。

title: 课程设置
content: 预期完成实证研究。如果由于某些原因,比如设法获准进入企业或者因为研究本身的耗时,收集数据需要很长的时间,那么实证研究最好在第二学年一开始就进行,甚至在第一学年末就着手。于第二年六月份,会进行第二学年的年度考核。

title: 跨越文化的全球领导
content: 在科研方面,从2007年开始她就是全球领导力与组织行为有效性科研项目小组成员,同时是该项目委员会成员。她领导了十几个由香港政府出资的科研项目,论文发表在《组织行为研究》,《领导学季刊》,《国际商业研究杂志》,《全球领导学研究动态》,《亚太管理杂志》,《欧洲应用心理学杂志》等国际性杂志上。

title: 大数据与决策
content:
目前,张教授正在研究电子商务与供应链管理的相关领域。 具体从事与大数据分析,线上及线下业务战略(例如新零售), 区块链业务模型和实验以及技术验收相关项目(例如:电子病历、工业标准 - Rosettanet、 RFID)。 与行业及公司紧密合作进行研究,例如趣链科技(中​​国的独角兽区块链公司之一)、唐泉金服,  中国人民银行,中国建设银行,京东,Mediviron Group of Clinics及阿里巴巴。
张教授在高管培训经验丰富,曾为中国中车、中航工业、鄞州银行,深圳城市规划局官员、宁波城市规划局官员及马来西亚管理学院等高管进行授课。

title: 企业战略
content: 他还曾担任荷兰能源委员会顾问,曾作为中国环境与发展国际合作委员会外国专家贡献了企业绿色发展社会责任政策研究。他目前担任由国务院发展研究中心及亚洲发展银行联合主办的关于中国制造业能效提升、排放控制及合规管理项目的外国专家。

title: 国际战略营销管理
content: 目前他还担任英国华威大学及英国特许市务学会特聘副研究员。他的主要研究领域为消费者行为学及品牌战略。基于其杰出的研究以及教学成就,他于2012年荣获宁波市政府颁发的优秀先进教师称号、诺丁汉大学全球校区杰出贡献奖 (Vice-Chancellor’s Achievement Award),并多次被英国诺丁汉郡提名迪林勋爵奖 (Lord Dearing Award)。

title: 建立高效国际化团队
content: 他曾被授予诸多教学奖章和荣誉,在超过15年的职业生涯中他培育了数千名学生和高管学员。

title: 创新:从创造到创业
content: 曹聪教授的研究得到美国国家科学基金会、欧盟、中国国家自然科学基金等的资助。他曾在剑桥大学出版社、Routledge Curzon等出版过专著,在世界著名学术期刊Science、Isis、Minerva、Research Policy、China Quarterly、Asian Survey等发表过大量研究论文,是国际知名的中国科技政策问题研究专家。

title: 运营和供应链战略
content: 同时,他还是电子产品及可持续运营生态设计专家。他曾担任政府资助项目“根据能源使用产品2005/32/EC号指令设计的电子产品生态设计及制造项目主管。陈庆佳教授曾在英国东安格利亚大学诺维奇商学院担任高级讲师,是英国工程技术学会(FIET)会士、英国高等教育学会(FHEA)会士、美国电气和电子工程师学会资深会员、英国国际物流与运输学会会员、认证工程师(CEng)。主要从事可持续运营与供应链管理、建模与分析、软计算技术在工业智能系统中的应用等研究。

title: 国际商务管理
content: 加入宁波诺丁汉大学之前,他曾在俄勒冈州波特兰大学和美国纽约佩斯大学任教,在中欧商学院(CEIBS)教授EMBA课程 。2010年到2016年期间,李教授担任过诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)副院长。李教授高管培训经验丰富,曾担任2012华润医药商业集团高级人才发展研修班主任,从2012年起每年为中国中车国际化人才高级培养项目授课。

title: 公司财务与战略管理
content: 他目前担任四本金融学主流国际期刊 (International Review of Financial Analysis, Finance Research Letters, International Review of Economics and Finance, Research in International Business and Finance) 的副主编和中国区域主编。迄今,他在国际主流金融,会计与经济学期刊上已发表论文20篇,其中18篇为英国ABS-3或澳大利亚ABDC-A排名期刊15篇为SSCI(包括9篇JCR-Q1)期刊论文。

title: 战略信息管理和电子商务
content:
周荫强教授以研究信息系统的应用、电子商务而闻名,他目前的研究领域涵盖:(1)企业如何在电子商务及社交媒体盛行的年代做得更好;(2)在电子商务环境及大数据年代中,企业如何做好信息安全管理;(3)利用大数据科技,助力企业发展更有效的商业运营模式。他研究的行业领域包括医疗行业、小型企业等诸多行业领域。 多年来,周荫强教授和世界各地的研究团队合作。 截至2020年3月,他的著作引用量在谷歌学术上逾20,000次,在商业研究领域位列亚洲最高引用量之一。他还在十多家国际学术期刊担任编辑委员,目前是信息与管理学术期刊《Information and Management》的主编,该期刊有近50年历史,是学术界公认的信息系统领域五大学术期刊之一。
在香港信息科技业界,香港计算机学会于2007年颁授周荫强教授为资深会员(Fellow),2008年至2011年期间委任其为副会长,2017年再次任命其为副会长。2013年至2017年,他担任香港信息科技专业认证局的认证委员会主席;2017年5月,被任命为董事会主席。香港信息科技专业认证局是香港唯一的信息科技专业认证机构。此外,周荫强亦应邀担任许多亚太区大型学术会议的首席演讲嘉宾,分享其见解及研究成果。 卓越的学术成就和社会贡献使周教授得到了多项任命和奖项的认可。2010年3月周荫强教授获中华人民共和国教育部长江学者讲座教授,2014年2月在香港大学获任命Padma and Hari Harilela战略信息管理教授。2014年9月在浙江大学获聘求是讲座教授,2017年9月在宁波诺丁汉大学担任李达三首席教授。他于2013年12月获颁发信息系统协会院士称号——每年在全球信息系统学科中不超过六名学者能获得此称号。他还应邀担任英国伦敦国王学院消费者与组织数据分析研究中心国际咨询委员会成员、台湾中正大学金融科技与数字治理研究中心国际咨询委员会成员以及大连理工大学管理与经济学部的国际咨询委员会成员。

title: 全球经济环境与金融风险
content: 刚纳斯教授自2007年加入宁波诺丁汉大学开始,积累了丰富的在经济学领域的教学经验。他的研究领域包括税费,外商直接投资和跨国企业,实验经济学和行为经济学。目前从事针对偷税漏税,中国的企业征税,跨国公司在中国的选址和中国的腐败的实验性研究,同时也研究税率竞争,中小企业融资和中国人的消费行为。他的部分工作已经和微数据有紧密联系并且用个体计量经济学分析这些数据。

title: 领导员工,打造团队,引领变革
content: 他在欧洲、亚洲、美国、中东和非洲国家地区有过丰富的工作经验,任职的企业包括英国最大的百货商店约翰·路易斯(John Lewis)、毕马威(KPMG)、美国管理系统(American Management Systems) 、沙宾特咨询公司(Sapient) 和里特咨询公司(Arthur·D·Little)等。洛克特教授还曾担任阿什里奇商学院的学术发展院长,带领推动阿什里奇商学院的国际化发展与合作。自2017年起,他被任命为诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)院长。洛克特教授在本科课程、研究生课程和MBA课程上有着丰富的执教经验。曾经执教的大学及商学院包括剑桥大学、牛津大学、帝国理工大学、公开大学、阿什里奇商学院,同时也在伦敦伯贝克学院和美国雪域大学担任访问教授。

title: Teaching and Learning
content: Our main undergraduate courses primarily aims at students on the Finance Accounting and Management (FAM) programme, but are available as compulsory or optional elements on other programmes. There are three modules providing an introduction to Financial Accounting, beginning with basic bookkeeping techniques and accounts preparation, later introducing consolidated accounts and in the final year considering a number of advanced accounting topics. Management accounting is covered over four modules – in the first two various computational techniques are explored, while final year modules look at the role of management accounting within organisations and the contribution it can make.

个人简介
邝国威教授(Professor Kok Wei Khong)现任诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)院长。在这之前,他曾是泰莱大学商业与法律学院的执行院长。在担任执行院长期间,泰莱商学院在商业与管理研究学科的QS世界大学学科排名从2019年的第300-350位跃升至2022年的第97位。他还带领泰莱商学院在12个月内通过了国际精英商学院协会初始自评报告(AASCB iSER),标志着该学院在获得AACSB全面认证的过程中取得了非常有效的进展。他曾担任诺丁汉大学马来西亚校区艺术与社会科学学院科研副院长,创建了跨学科数据分析中心,该中心在成立10个月后的2018年底实现了自我维持运营。
邝国威教授在学术界工作了20多年,专注于服务营销、用户技术接受度研究、社交媒体研究、行为科学、商业分析、机器学习和流程再造等领域的研究。他的研究成果发表在《信息与管理(Information and Management)》、《服务营销杂志(Journal of Services Marketing)》、《专家系统与应用(Expert Systems with Applications)》、《供应链管理:国际期刊(Supply Chain Management: An International Journal)》、《工业管理与数据系统(Industrial Management and Data Systems)》、《计算机信息系统杂志(Journal of Computer Information Systems)》、《商业伦理学杂志(Journal of Business Ethics)》、《商业战略与环境(Business Strategy and the Environment)》等极具影响力的顶级期刊上。

个人简介
陈致玮博士是哥本哈根商学院(CBS)数字化系教授,宁波诺丁汉大学中国校区(UNNC)商学院的国际商务分析与数字化荣誉教授,中国科学技术大学(USTC)管理学院客座教授,Weizenbaum网络社会研究所高级研究员,悉尼新南威尔士大学信息系统与技术管理学院访问教授研究员。他获得了不列颠哥伦比亚大学的工商管理博士学位(专攻管理信息系统)。他的研究兴趣集中在与数字服务相关的设计和创新问题上,研究成果发表在MIS Quarterly(MISQ),信息系统研究(ISR),管理信息系统期刊(JMIS),信息系统协会期刊(JAIS),美国信息科学与技术学会期刊(JASIST),欧洲信息系统期刊(EJIS),决策支持系统(DSS),信息与管理(I&M)等领先的同行评审期刊上。除了被任命为MISQ的高级编辑之外,Chee-Wee博士还担任MISQ,I&M,Internet Research(IntR)和Journal of Management Analytics(JMA)的副主编。此外,目前Chee Wee博士在工业管理与数据系统(IMDS)、工程管理(IEEE-TEM)、JAIS和计算机信息系统杂志(JCIS)的编委会任职,同时担任DSS、I&M和JMIS处理各类特殊问题的编委。最后,Chee-Wee博士是CBS与上海交通大学安泰经济与管理学院(ACEM)联合研究中心的联席主任。
教学
陈致玮博士在哥伦比亚广播公司(CBS)教授本科与研究生的课程。具体而言,他所教授的本科课程中涵盖了与创新技术相关的主题。而对于研究生课程,他则向学生介绍了方法论实践的最新进展和趋势。此外,陈致玮博士还在CBS的高管暑期学校讲授数字平台战略,该校面向高级企业管理层。
研究方向
陈致玮博士的主要研究领域集中在与各种环境下的数字服务交付相关的设计和创新问题上(例如,电子商贸,电子商务,电子政务,电子医疗,电子市场和移动电子商务)。他尤为感兴趣的是如何从数字服务中提取价值,以及探索当代技术趋势(例如,人工智能(AI),大数据,区块链,游戏化,物联网(IoT)和社交媒体等,从而为创新服务设计做出贡献。
研究兴趣
数字服务设计相关各方面:
便利性,质量,故障和恢复
大数据分析和服务创新
区块链驱动服务创新
情境感知服务创新
游戏化和服务创新
物联网(IoT)和服务创新
群体平台的服务创新
金融技术领域的服务创新
社交网络中的服务创新
荣誉职位
MISQ,I&M,IntR及JMA副主编
DSS、I&M及JMIS编委

袁睿志博士于 2011 年和 2016 年在英国诺丁汉大学和诺丁汉大学商学院分别获得硕士(一等)学位和博士学位。袁博士目前任职于宁波诺丁汉大学市场营销学讲师。其主要研究领域包括:绿色消费、市场营销创新、共享旅游、社会化媒体营销以及品牌营销等,近三年来曾在国际前沿会议及期刊发表论文近 20 篇及专著书目两本。
袁睿志博士多年来担任市场营销基础学、消费者行为学等本科课程的教学,在加入宁波诺丁汉大学之前,还于西交利物浦大学担任市场营销学讲师与工商管理项目主任,擅于互动式教学,凭借出色的教学理念与风格深受学生的喜爱。袁博士还参与多项高管培训营销课程管理及其课程编排。除此之外,还身兼多个组织和学校社团指导,力求帮助学生更快速、更有效地取得长足进步及全面发展。
袁睿志博士近年来先后获得国家自然科学基金青年科学基金项目及省级、校级研究发展项目,迄今已在 Journal  of  Business  Research,  Supply  Chain  Management:  An International Journal,  Advances in Consumer Research 等期刊上发表论文 10 余篇, 还于 2014 年获欧洲市场营销学会十佳论文奖励。

个人简介
米凯莱·杰拉奇教授作为意大利经济发展部前副部长,负责国际贸易和投资。在此之前,他在中国生活了10年,期间在中国的许多大学担任宏观经济学家和金融学教授。在2008年移居中国之前,杰拉奇在伦敦生活了20年,20年间他担任了伦敦金融城的顶级电信投资银行家及电子工程师。2018年曾被提名为意大利总理的候选人之一,后出任意大利经济发展部副部长。他还是国际主流媒体的常客,并被意大利总统马塔雷拉授予意大利之星骑士勋章。他拥有麻省理工学院斯隆管理学院的工商管理硕士学位,精通涵盖中文在内的五种语言。
自2018年6月起,杰拉奇先生担任副国务卿期间同时意大利经济发展部(Conte I Administration)负责国际贸易和投资。由于他在中国的专长,在2018年3月习近平主席访问意大利期间,他是意大利和中国签署的首份G7 “一带一路”MOU 的主要建筑师。在担任副国务卿的第一年,他成立了一个“中国特别工作组”,这是一个跨部委的论坛,旨在交流意见和制定改善与中国贸易的商业战略,并制定了一项新的基于系统的战略,采用核心和卫星方式在世界各地推销意大利产品。针对猖獗的贸易自由化倾向于惩罚最弱和最不灵活的国家这一现象,杰拉奇教授成立了一个分析自由贸易协定的工作队,量化每一个自由贸易协定的经济影响,这是意大利以前从未做过的研究。作为副国务卿,他在二十国集团(G20)等所有国际政府活动中发挥了比以往更加积极的作用,以确保意大利的利益得到最好的体现。该项活动的全部摘要可在网站
www.michelegeraci.com
获取。
2008年至2018年,杰拉奇先生就居于中国,担任金融学教授和经济学家。他是诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)金融政策学教授(专业技术),是全球政策研究所中国区负责人,纽约大学、上海和浙江大学金融学的兼职教授。最近,杰拉奇先生还被北京大学经济学院授予名誉教授职务。他的研究工作面向政府、企业和投资者,提供非学术性、面向实际的政策建议和投资建议。他们感兴趣的话题包括货币政策、收入差距、移民、城市化和欧洲危机、国际贸易、并购。作为一名中国经济学家,杰拉奇连续五年被米兰金融公司(MilanoFinanza)评选为意大利对华事务50强专家之一。他还为罗马路易斯敦商学院(LUISS)(罗马)、哥本哈根商学院(Copenhagen Business School)和纽约大学斯特恩香港科技大学(NYU Stern HKUST)的全球金融硕士课程中讲授中国经济在欧洲的课程。不仅仅作为该纪录片的制作人和主持人,他还有一个很受欢迎的博客,旨在增进欧洲和意大利的决策者、 企业和公众对中国的了解。
在进入中国之前,他曾在伦敦担任投资银行家,专门从事电信媒体技术行业(TMT)。从伦敦到华尔街之间的十年间,他曾在欧洲、拉丁美洲、东欧等投资银行工作过,如美林、美国银行、DLJ,先是在公司融资团队进行IPO和并购,后来又担任卖方电信分析师,欧洲电信研究联席主管兼拉丁美洲电信研究主管,最后调到施罗德投资管理公司负责电信投资的买方,在国际金融危机爆发之前,他怀着从微观转换到宏观经济分析的愿望,离开了伦敦前往上海。
在进入金融行业之前,杰拉奇先生曾在英国电信(British Telecom)伦敦卫星规划部担任电子工程师。他为参与了欧洲通信卫星热鸟卫星的设计而感到自豪。因现如今,这些卫星今天被用来向欧洲广播电视。
杰拉奇先生在莫迪利亚尼教授和鲁迪•多恩布施的指导和友谊下,获得了麻省理工学院斯隆管理学院(M.I.T .Sloan School of Management)的MBA学位,在意大利巴勒莫大学(University of Palermo)获得电子工程学士学位,并在伦敦大学学院(UCL)作为交换生学习了一年,掌握了意大利语、英语、汉语、西班牙语和一些法语。

title: Charles Yichu Wang 博士
content:
Charles Yichu Wang博士是诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)金融学助理教授。他的主要研究领域是公司金融、创新创业、创业金融、房地产以及中国经济等。他的研究成果发表于
Management Science
、
Review of Corporate Finance Studies
等知名国际期刊,并入选众多高水平学术会议进行宣讲,包括SFS Cavalcade、ABFER、FMA、AsianFA、CES North America以及中国经济学年会和中国金融学年会等。他还有评论性和综述性文章及相关访谈刊载于《中国金融》、《清华金融评论》、《西班牙五日报》等媒体。他担任了多个高水平期刊的匿名审稿人,包括
Journal of Corporate Finance
、
Journal of Banking and Finance
、
Corporate Governance:An International Review
等。学术研究之外,他还是一名专业作曲人、钢琴家、乐队指挥、以及创业者和风险投资人,其作品多次在国家大剧院、国家图书馆、中山音乐堂及世界各地演出,他也带领团队多次参加各大国际音乐节并获奖,其中包括佛罗伦萨国际音乐节两枚金牌。

个人简介
冯昍博士 (Dr Xuan Feng) 是诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)人力资源管理与组织行为学副教授。她在德国慕尼黑大学获得了社会与管理心理学的博士学位。其主要研究领域包括:领导力评估和培训、员工健康管理、人力资源管理、职业生涯发展、国际人才的引进和培养、组织和工作设计等。冯昍博士在国际知名学术和应用类管理期刊上发表与人才管理相关论文,目前是美国管理学会、中国管理研究国际学会以及欧洲管理心理学学会会员,并在上述三大管理学会年会上均有著作发表。
冯昍博士具有丰富的政府课题研究经验,作为课题负责人完成了多个市级和区级的人才政策课题项目,由其负责完成的人才研究课题报告两项被收入《宁波市人才蓝皮书》,一项获得市级嘉奖,并于2020年获得英国诺丁汉大学政策研究中心授予的“政策研究冉生新星”特别嘉奖。冯昍博士曾在多个政府组织的人才研讨会上做主题演讲,其研究报告作为决策建议被用于市级和区级政府人才政策的制定。
在宁波诺丁汉大学,冯昍博士主要教授人力资源管理课程,先后获得诺丁汉大学最高级别个人杰出贡献奖—校长执行奖章(Vice Chancellor’s Medal)和最高级别教学杰出贡献奖—迪林勋爵教学奖 (Lord Dearing Award)。其开发的商学院学生职业发展教育项目获得2020年度宁波市高等教育突出成果奖。冯昍博士有丰富的高管培训经验,在留德期间,曾担任全德国排名第一的慕尼黑工业大学EMBA项目的兼职讲师,为CEO级别的欧洲高管讲授跨国领导力、人力资源和中国管理艺术。在宁波诺丁汉大学,冯昍博士担任高管培训项目讲师,讲授跨国人力资源管理、变革管理、工作设计和领导力方面内容。在教课培训之外,冯昍博士具有企业咨询和一对一及团队教练辅导经验,帮助学生和管理者提升职业能力和领导力,为组织提供优化管理方案。
在就职于诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)之前,冯昍博士先后任职于多家大型德国知名企业,主要从事人才培养、领导力发展、组织变革和海外招聘等相关工作。结合实验方法与商业实践,冯昍博士在企业内部开展调研,并为公司和管理层在领导力和人力资源管理等专业领域提供咨询服务。

title: 重点研究领域与课题
content:
重点研究领域与课题
重点领域一:可持续食物系统与农业转型研究
全球气候变化、食品安全和农村可持续发展等挑战性问题迫切需要建构可持续的食物系统,它有依赖于农业系统的转型,涉及到技术、社会和体制(或政策)等诸多子系统(或要素)的创新及其匹配协同。本网络从系统性创新的视角出发,聚焦在全球5亿多小农(中国占一半)如何实现生产方式转型这一核心问题,试图研究和理解中国等发展中国家在农村社区层面所面临的多重挑战、机遇及其成功成功的案例、经验,进而揭示实现可持续食物系统、农业转型的可选择的路径、模式、条件及其·政策建议。基于已有的青年研究者兴趣和相匹配的导师团队,现阶段重点支持(但不局限于)如下课题:
1.1
可持续替代生计系统与农村可持续发展
1.2
中国乡村振兴的区域类型与创新战略研究
重点领域二:中英合作创新基地建设与产业振兴研究
第三世界的国家的可持续食物系统建构与农业转型需要改革或重塑农业创新系统、高等教育系统,以推动当地的产业振兴,实现脱贫和可持续生计目标。本研究方向旨在总结中国不同农业生态区在“精准扶贫”、“乡村振兴”实施过程中所面临的挑战性问题和创新机构、人员“对口帮扶”的成功经验,为青年学者同各类利益相关者发展合作提供新的思路,帮助他们更好地理解地方主导产业升级、产品或服务标准化和市场化过程中的需求、动力、资源和机遇。基于同相关机构、组织、企业业已建立起来的合作关系,现阶段的重点研究项目包括:
2.1
边缘地区马铃薯产业化与国际化研究
2.2
第三世界可持续食物系统的理论与实践
2.3
龙头企业在中国小农转型、市场对接中的作研究
2.4
生态脆弱区生态农业发展和农村转型的路径研究
研究方向三:社会创新和企业家成长研究
在发展中国家城镇化、人才流失和乡村衰退的背景下,通过外部参与或干预方式,强化人力资本和社会资本,是实现可持续脱贫和乡村转型成功的重要条件。然而,同对自上而下的外部干预和技术创新的研究和强调相比,我们对社会创新,即农村人口如何转变态度、观念、行为方式,进而发展共同利益、身份认同和有效利用各类资源、机遇的集体行动等方面,却知之甚少。在这方面,中国的“精准扶贫”和正在实施的“乡村振兴”战略,为学术研究提供了丰富的信息和大量成功案例,有助于我们理解社会创新、企业家成长、自下而上发展及其同外部干预的有效衔接。现阶段我们重点支持(但不局限于)如下研究主题:
3.1
边缘地区建构伙伴关系、发展乡村旅游的模式研究
3.2
中国社区林业的转型及其生态和社会效益研究

title: Impact Hub
content:
Impact Hub
The CFRS encourages and supports ECRs to engage with multiple stakeholders to promote the vision and mission of CFRS. This Hub aims to promote public awareness about the challenges and good practices in sustainable food and rural transition in China and global south through blogs written by CFRS members or reports of relevant events via weblinks (with a bilingual title and short description).
Background of the CFRS:
The origin of the CFRS can be traced back to “Farmer innovation system in the Loess Plateau of China” (2009-2010), a part of UK’s ESPA Programme (Ecosystem Services and Poverty Alleviation). The idea was further developed through an international workshop on “Global-local knowledge system for rural innovation and entrepreneurship in the developing world” (2019) and enriched by a GCRF Pilot Project: “Cooperative ecosystem to empower small farmers in the poor areas of China” (2020).
Thanks to the Newton-NSFC ECR Links Workshop Grant, “Systematic innovation for food security and rural sustainability”, this project attracted 41 ECRs mainly from UK and China. To cope with the interruption by Covid-19 Pandemic, a series of pre-workshop activities were arranged online for ECRs to meet mentors and stakeholder representatives via group meeting, methodological salons and roundtable meetings. The above preparation provides a sound base for
UK-China ECR Links Workshop
(8-9/12/2021) with aims to establish the CFRS through keynote speeches, ECR presentations and roundtable discussions. For the detailes of project implementation, research findings and outcomes, please see the report.

title: NUBS China professor shares views on attracting students studying abroad to return to Ningbo for entrepreneurship and employment
content:
On 9 May, Dr Xiaodan Yu, Assistant Professor of Entrepreneurship and Innovation at Nottingham University Business School China (NUBS China), was invited to participate in the Zhejiang Provincial Youth Innovation and Entrepreneurship Competition Launch Ceremony and the Yongjiang Science and Technology Innovation Youth Talent Summit. Dr Xiaodan Yu gave her unique insights on how university students can make career plans in entrepreneurship and innovation, and how to attract more students studying aboard to return to China for employment and entrepreneurship. By introducing cutting-edge business concepts from around the world and cultivating international business talents, NUBS China has been committed to fostering local economic development and promoting Ningbo's high-level construction as the "Global Capital of Intelligent Manufacturing and Innovation".
As an Assistant Professor of Entrepreneurship and Innovation at the University of Nottingham Ningbo China, what qualities do you think are needed for university students to be young innovative entrepreneurs or how should they properly plan their career in entrepreneurship and innovation?
In terms of the personality traits of entrepreneurs, students with the following three qualities generally have stronger entrepreneurial intentions and better entrepreneurial performance.
Firstly, there is "openness" and this refers to students maintaining an open attitude towards external experiences and knowledge, possessing a strong curiosity, imagination, creativity and a certain level of adventurousness.
Secondly, a "sense of responsibility" refers to students being able to complete their plans with great self-discipline, care and organisation. And after completing an objective, there is a strong sense of achievement.
Thirdly, 'extroversion' refers to traits such as confidence, talkativeness and energy that students need to have. There is also a life and work philosophy that expresses, "Believe in me, I can accomplish it."
The personality traits I mentioned above can be gradually formed through cultivation and exercise. Therefore, we can stimulate entrepreneurial enthusiasm in students through innovation and entrepreneurship modules and competitions at the university. Through the process of learning and practice, students can initially cultivate and discover their entrepreneurial qualities. For example, NUBS China offers the compulsory module Entrepreneurship Theory and Practice to all year two students. This module provides undergraduate students with the opportunity to explore and discover problems. These 'problems' are actually 'pain points' in the market, and tackling them is also an opportunity for entrepreneurship.
Furthermore, the entrepreneurial environment of the wider society will also stimulate the entrepreneurial vitality of university students. As one of the most active cities for private enterprise in China, Ningbo has its own entrepreneurial culture and impact. Of course, the government, research institutions, universities and enterprises need to jointly create an active innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystem.
You have many years of experience visiting and studying abroad. What do you think is the biggest difference between the innovative and entrepreneurial environment for young people abroad and in China? How can we attract more students studying abroad to return to China for employment and entrepreneurship?
The innovative and entrepreneurial environment varies among different countries and regions. For example, many European countries lack an environment for innovation and entrepreneurship, making it difficult to create unicorn companies. However, the United States can continuously generate highly influential unicorn companies, such as ChatGPT, launched by the American company OpenAI, which was born in Silicon Valley, San Francisco. This place gathers the best universities in the world, such as Stanford University and the University of California, Berkeley, and with its many national research institutions, attracts the world's best talents. It also has the most experienced high-tech venture capitalists. All these factors constitute a very complete innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystem. At the same time, advanced entrepreneurial education concepts have also emerged in the local area because entrepreneurship education is closely related to local technological innovation and the industrial structure.
The key to attracting more students studying abroad to return to China for employment and entrepreneurship lies in creating an innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystem based on the local industrial structure and its advantages. This system requires high-quality foundations, basic and applied research institutions, talent training institutions, efficient financial service institutions, high-quality infrastructure (such as digital infrastructure), high-quality large enterprises and a relatively relaxed institutional environment to provide space for students studying abroad to innovate and start businesses. These factors complement each other in an innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystem.

3D打印时代, 中英两国三地共议如何保护数字知识产权
2023年04月12日
为推动数字知识产权保护和智能制造发展,3月25日和28日,“智能制造和数字知识产权保护暨诺印3D模型鉴权平台推介会”分别于宁波索菲特大酒店和上海复旦大学举行。本次会议由英国艺术与人文研究理事会(AHRC),诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)及英国埃克塞特法学院联合举办,并得到AHRC后续基金及李达三创新基金的支持。会议由中国会场和英国会场组成,中国会场由宁波会场及上海分会场组成。本次会议吸引了来自高校、科研机构、制造业企业和律师事务所等一百余名专家学者通过线上和线下的方式共同参会。
随着人工智能、云计算、区块链、5G通信以及数字水印等新一代数字技术不断为智能制造领域注入新活力,由这些前沿技术衍生的知识产权也在全球经济中扮演着越来越重要的角色。那么,如何进行数字知识产权保护就成了智能制造领域一个非常关键的前沿问题。
宁波会场
宁波诺丁汉大学科研及知识交流副校长周荫强教授向到场的嘉宾和观众表达了热烈的欢迎并为此次活动致开幕词。周教授肯定了此次活动的重要意义,知识产权保护在当下技术革新和产业变革的背景下显得尤为的重要。
来自英国埃克塞特大学的James Griffin教授和来自诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)的慕晓琛博士,在法律层面从比较法的方向,阐释了在数字经济时代,传统的法学理论研究应如何应对新兴技术带来的挑战。James 教授展示了数字水印技术在3D打印领域的应用,数字水印技术可以很好的解决数字模型的权利归属问题,无论是从权利拥有者的角度还是从平台的角度,数字水印技术都起着举足轻重的作用。紧接着,慕晓琛博士以人工智能时代独创性判断标准的坚守为切入点,在介绍了世界上各国的相关理论的基础上,展望了在未来法律可以和技术的进步达成完美的平衡。
区块链融合技术专家郝雷博士结合他在区块链科技企业任职期间积累的丰富实践经验,探讨了区块链技术可能对中国电影产业带来的影响。视频区块链技术,有望高效地保护知识产权,并遏制盗版现象,为电影人创造更多的展映机会,从而助力电影产业的蓬勃发展。
随后,诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)教学与学生体验副院长、运营管理学教授陈庆佳和诺印产品经理郭珉详细介绍了诺印(Nottink)平台。诺印平台依靠于已持有的3D打印模型数字水印专利技术和区块链技术,利用平台化、系统化、流程化优势,为商业终端客户提供便捷可靠的3D打印加密鉴权平台。
会上,宁波市律师协会涉外与一带一路专业委员会委员,北京大成(宁波)律师事务所合伙人王缇莹律师和浙江省律师协会知识产权专业委员会主任、北京大成(宁波)律师事务所高级合伙人黄妙律师,就诺印鉴权平台的功能进行了深入点评和讨论,他们普遍认为诺印平台作为智能制造中3D打印细分领域的知识产权保护方案非常具有前景优势,并且能促进3D打印行业可持续和良性发展。
英国会场
来自英国的数位专家也就技术与法律的融合从不同的角度做了精彩的分享。Angela教授和Kwaku Adu-Admankwa博士从生产链的角度进一步解释法律与技术的关系,他们认为法律的规定并不会阻碍技术的进步,法律的制定反而是为了保障相关制度的具体实施以及避免不必要的纠纷。
Phoebe Li博士分享了在生物技术领域需要面对和解决的法律问题。Onyeka教授将传统的合同法理论与自动授权技术相融合,进一步阐释了合同在自动授权领域的应用。最后牟雅沁博士从财产权理论入手,阐释了3D打印模型的著作权保护的可行性和必要性,从而进一步深化了法律与技术的融合。
上海分会场
上海分会场由复旦大学法学院、复旦大学知识产权研究中心以及宁波诺丁汉大学商学院联合主办,会议从法律视角热烈探讨了3D打印、智能制造与数字知识产权的保护问题。会议由陈庆佳教授和复旦大学法学院、复旦大学知识产权研究中心常务副主任马忠法教授联合主持。复旦大学法学院副院长杜宇教授致欢迎词,他指出,技术革新与智能制造对法律制度带来了新问题、新变化,其中典型之一是知识产权认定客体的拓宽与界定困难,使得知识产权的侵权行为更加隐蔽。
会议上半场以数字知识产权法律问题为主题。华东理工大学法学院讲师刘慧博士针对构建数据知识产权分类分级保护机制进行了探讨与研究成果分享。她指出当前数据知识产权治理和确权问题亟待解决,以促进数据创新、保护个人隐私和推动数据共享。她强调可以从实践需求出发推动理论不断发展,并总结了当前已有的数据知识产权保护的基本原则与规范、分级分类标准及保护绩效评估机制。
上海政法学院经济法学院副教授、经济法学院丝绸之路律师学院执行院长商建刚,结合丰富的数据交易和知识产权保护的实践经验,就“认定数据权益的理论与制度进路”为主题进行了分享,充分反思了当前数据赋权的双面性,并建议提出“数据产品制作者权”的全新概念。
上海财经大学上海国际组织与全球治理研究院助理研究员厉言冰以“大数据与数据盗用”为主题,分享了大数据的特性,特别是其与被盗用相关的特性及其导致的数据保护的相关问题。她介绍和比较了当前国际国内针对不同客体的大数据反盗用相关的法律法规,及大数据反盗用与现有相关法律法规的交互处理方式。
由马忠法教授主持的下半场会议聚焦于3D打印领域的知识产权法律问题。同济大学上海国际知识产权学院助理教授王玉凯博士探讨了制作和传播3D打印数字模型的知识产权法规制,他强调了数字模型制作和传播在3D打印技术实施和法律认定中的重要地位,对数字模型的法律性质进行了定性,并提出了对未来不同情形下数字模型制作和传播的法律责任的认定建议。
马忠法教授探讨了3D打印中的合理使用与侵权认定,他提出了3D打印侵权的各领域认定标准建议,建议使用必要的技术保护措施防范3D打印的侵权行为,并提出了未来侵权行为的法规表述修改及举证责任倒置等建议。
本次会议是智能制造和数字知识产权保护的盛会,表现了国内企业对数字知识产权保护的社会责任及其对智能制造发展的重视。这也为智能制造领域的专家和企业提供了一个共享经验、了解最新技术发展的平台。

业界大咖、优秀校友、公司代表...这个活动你没来就真亏了
2023年04月07日
3月25日,诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)的学生实践和职业发展计划正式启动。
该计划旨在为学生提供更多锻炼专业技能的机会,探索职业规划,并通过多种方式提高他们的就业能力。通过这一计划,学生有机会将他们的知识和技能应用于现实世界的问题和场景,并被介绍给可以协助他们职业发展的行业专家和雇主。
在本次启动活动中,诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)特别邀请到德勤中国税务合伙人叶红女士为同学们做了一场主题演讲。叶红女士不仅分享了许多咨询行业的最新发展情况,而且还给同学们提供了许多非常实用的面试技巧。
叶红女士直接参与德勤招聘工作多年,她表示,
对于应届生,公司会考虑你已掌握的技能,但会更看重应聘者的气质和潜力,尤其是分析能力和极限抗压能力。面试时,如果被问到一些特别刁钻的问题,千万不能慌,乱了阵脚。这个时候,公司想得到的并不是一个正确的答案,而是通过这类问题考察学生的分析能力以及抗压能力。如果你能镇定地、思路清晰地拆分难题,那肯定是可以得到加分的。
此外,应聘者还需要对自己申请的职位表现出真正的兴趣,并且拥有一个自圆其说、令人信服的说法。如果面试官感觉到,你对申请的职位并不是太了解,也没有足够的热情,而仅仅是想找一份工作,那肯定对你的印象会大打折扣。
宁波诺丁汉大学党委副书记、副校长沈伟其以及教学与学生体验副校长Philip Seltsikas也亲临活动现场并发言。他们不仅充分肯定了商学院在提高学生实践体验上所做的努力,也鼓励学生们积极参与其中,把课堂所学运用到实践当中去,提高就业能力,为将来的职业发展打下坚实基础。
诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)院长邝国威教授和教学与学生体验副院长陈庆佳教授在活动现场表示,商学院一直致力于培养“实战型”商业精英,特别注重与商界的直接联系,确保学生课堂所学与实际商业紧密关联。
在活动的下午场,诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)教育伙伴关系主任王仪博士进行了致辞,学生专业实践项目负责人黄琳博士对学生实践与职业发展计划进行了详细介绍。
宁诺校友、现安永博智隆战略咨询经理张博弈还跟学弟学妹们分享了自己的职业感悟。
张博弈认为,对于很多人来说,拥有一个清晰的自我认知和对世界的认知并不是一件容易的事情,有时候“自由而无用”的探索也是必由之路,尤其是在大学期间。在对自我的探索中,努力找到自己的偏好、热情和理想,与此同时,通过提问、求证和讨论交流,搞清这个世界的运行规律。然后把二者结合,这样才能找到真正适合自己一生的职业方向。
下午场还分别进行了面向金融财务与管理和国际商务两个专业的企业宣讲。交通银行、宁波银行、中信证券、广博集团股份有限公司、宁波惠尔顿婴童安全科技股份有限公司以及浙江动一新能源动力科技股份有限公司的代表分别做了讲演,并与同学们进行了现场交流。
国际商务专场的三家企业还提供了管培生的职位,他们也提到了关于本土企业对于人才的需求,并表示希望未来能有机会和宁诺学生有更多交流。
学生实践和职业发展计划目前已有十个项目。在下午场的活动中,所有项目的负责老师也全部来到现场,与同学们交流并回答相关咨询(SEED Scheme Mingle Session)。
由诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)与大华会计事务所合建的财务会计类教育培训实习基地——诺华大学生实践教育基地,最近被评为“省级大学生校外实践教育基地”。接下来,学生实践和职业发展计划将依托诺华大学生实践教育基地开展系列活动。
诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)的学生实践和职业发展计划还会推出一系列活动,我们也会通过本平台第一时间向大家发布相关信息。

PMI高校合作奖!NUBS China携手国际行业协会,助力学生职业发展
2023年03月29日
3月17日,宁波诺丁汉大学在北京被美国项目管理协会(中国)授予2023年度注册教育机构“高校合作奖”。这是对诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)多年来坚持引进国际前沿的项目管理课程,为中国企业培养“实战型”项目管理精英人才的一次充分肯定。
美国项目管理协会(Project Management Institute,简称PMI)成立于1969年,是一个由项目管理专业领域内的研究人员、学者、顾问和经理组成的全球性的专业权威机构,目前在全球185个多国家拥有超过85万名会员和证书持有人。
宁波诺丁汉大学是PMI的注册教育机构,这意味着诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)所提供的相关课程不仅达到或超过了PMI在质量和有效性方面所制定的严格标准,并且可以颁发培训学时数,以满足PMI的项目管理专业人士资质认证考试对相关培训的要求。
PMI的项目管理专业人士资质认证(Project Management Professional,简称PMP)具有广泛的国际影响力,是项目管理领域在全球通用的权威认证,并受到大部分世界500强企业的青睐。持有PMP证书已经成为很多公司招聘项目经理的硬性条件。
诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)还计划将PMP课程加入到未来的企业高管培训当中,直接帮助企业培养项目管理人才。通过PMP课程的培训,企业人才可以在简化工作流程、提高工作效率、降低运营成本、增强竞争力等方面,获取国际最先进的理念和方法。
诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)一直秉持“国际化、互动式、创新型”的教育理念,积极引进国际权威的行业资质认证课程和培训,不仅让学生掌握最先进的商业管理理念,还能助力学生通过专业考试获得各类行业资质,增强个人就业竞争力,获得更快速的职业发展。
除了PMI,诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)还与多个国际行业协会有深入合作,比如金融财会类专业的毕业生,在参加ACCA(特许公认会计师公会专业考试计划)、ICAEW(英格兰与威尔士特许会计师协会专业阶段)、CPA Australia(澳大利亚注册会计师公会)及CIMA(特许管理会计师公会商业会计证书)等的行业资质考试时,都可以获得一定科目免试。
诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)的金融投资类专业还是CFA Institute (特许金融分析师协会)认可的CFA课程合作伙伴专业(University Affiliation Program),课程设置紧密贴合金融投资行业实务并且有助于学生准备CFA考试。
此外,诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)的国际管理(市场营销)专业还获得英国特许市场营销协会(CIM)的认证,该协会是全球市场营销人员的领先专业机构。该专业的学生在学习硕士课程的同时,还有机会获得剑桥营销学院颁发的CIM专业市场营销文凭。据调查显示,持有CIM证书的毕业生,平均薪水比普通市场营销毕业生的起薪高20%,而且更容易获得晋升。

中国+英国+马来西亚,诺丁汉大学商学院三校联动构建全球合作平台
2023年03月15日
3月8日至10日,第三届诺丁汉大学商学院三校会议成功举行。来自诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)、诺丁汉大学商学院(英国)和诺丁汉大学商学院(马来西亚)200余位学术教师和博士生,汇聚在这一高水平的全球科研合作平台,进行经验分享和学术交流。
诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)院长邝国威教授表示:此次三校会议为学者们提供了一个重要而又独特的机会去探究商业管理领域的最新研究进展。
“
众所周知,数字化和数据分析正改变着我们的商业方式。从人工智能到区块链,越来越多的公司依赖数字工具提高效率、简化流程并提高客户体验。在被数字化引领的后疫情时代,我们必须走到一起,真正分享我们的想法,了解研究的未来机会
。”
本次会议共收到论文近60篇,其中由博士生和老师合著的论文就占了半数以上。诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)科研与知识交流副院长刘任远教授表示,这充分体现了诺丁汉大学商学院浓厚的学术氛围和对人才培养的重视。
为期三天的诺丁汉大学商学院三校会议涵括数字化和数据分析、会计学、金融市场、供应链等多个学科领域。与会者分组参与了论文的陈述和讨论,分享个人或团体正在进行的研究并了解其他同事目前正在从事的研究课题,从而发掘潜在的合作可能性,促进三校间就某些领域和课题形成研究集群。
此外,与会者还有机会在会议中获取有关科研项目和论文的建议和反馈,以及向科研会议和学术期刊提交论文的针对性建议。会议通过高水平的学术交流,帮助学者们拓展学术视野,激发研究思路。
诺丁汉大学商学院三校会议是打通三校间科研合作交流的一个重要平台。诺丁汉大学商学院(英国)和诺丁汉大学商学院(马来西亚)对本次会议也高度重视。
英国诺丁汉大学社会科学学院副校长Todd Landman教授表示,与诺丁汉大学致力于打造“无边界的大学”的战略目标一致,诺丁汉大学商学院(英国)的愿景是贯彻无边界的商业理念。该学院也正努力加强三校合作,利用诺丁汉大学独特的三校位置进一步强化国际化教学与科研发展。
诺丁汉大学马来西亚校区艺术与社会科学学院院长、诺丁汉大学商学院(马来西亚)代理院长Jason Pandya Wood博士也强调:该会议不仅仅是一个学术会议,对教学发展和课程建设同样具有重要意义。
通过紧密的三校联动,学者和学生可以获得在世界三大地区(全球第二大经济体的中国、英国所处的欧洲、马来西亚所处的东盟)拓展经验的机会。这无论是在中国还是在全球范围,都很少有商学院能够提供这样的机会。本次三校会议的成功举办,再次彰显了诺丁汉大学作为一所真正国际化大学的独特优势。

title: 校企联动新典范 – “新秀丽青年英才进修培训项目”首批学员顺利毕业

校企联动新典范 – “新秀丽青年英才进修培训项目”首批学员顺利毕业
2023年02月23日
2月18日,在诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)的教授们和新秀丽(中国)有限公司管理高层的共同见证下,“新秀丽青年英才进修培训项目”的首批学员,经过三个阶段的紧张学习之后顺利毕业。
“新秀丽青年英才进修培训项目”是宁波诺丁汉大学践行校企联动的又一典范。该项目依托宁诺的国际化教育资源,旨在提升新秀丽(中国)有限公司青年人才的商务综合能力,通过三阶段的定制课程,帮助学员了解自我,了解当今变革时代,从而加深对新秀丽(中国)组织与战略的理解。课程内容以专业理论性知识为基础,借鉴行业最佳实践与案例,推动学员完成知识与经验的融合,重塑新的商业认知与思维,为新秀丽的发展注入新力量。
毕业典礼在宁波诺丁汉大学国际创业创新大楼举行。诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)院长邝国威教授致开场辞。他提到,“我们相信,教育不仅仅是知识的获取,更是培养应对复杂挑战、积极推动变革所需的技能、信心和适应能力。希望通过这次高管培训项目,学员们不仅对商业知识有更加全面系统的了解,而且也对自己和周围的世界有更深刻的认识。”
邝国威教授鼓励学员们庆祝自己的成功,并肩负起自己作为杰出团队群体中一员的责任,希望他们能够灵活运用习得的商业知识和世界洞见,在未来继续大放异彩,回馈社会。
在毕业典礼上,新秀丽(中国)六个课题小组一一进行了毕业成果汇报,对其在数字化、新消费背景下的转型与发展进行了大胆的构想与规划。成果汇报不仅内容紧扣课题,展现形式也是创意多样,学员们使用短剧、对谈、辩论等形式,新奇生动地通过案例展示了在课程中获得的知识,充分展现了培训后的崭新风采,受到了现场嘉宾的高度评价。
新秀丽集团大中华区总裁马瑞国先生对学员们的学习成长也非常满意,他表示很荣幸能够和宁波诺丁汉大学达成合作,为公司的可持续发展培养优秀的高潜力人才。马先生同样强调了学以致用的重要性,“知易行难,我希望各位学员不但要保持这样的学习精神,持之以恒的学习,更要学以致用,把培训期间获得的启发和思考应用到实际工作中去,希望各位在未来成为公司的中流砥柱。”
学员陈寿康分享了在整个项目周期的学习收获,他表示和各位学员、老师的相遇是一段美好的经历,让他受益匪浅。在他对课程时光的娓娓回忆和对老师和公司的衷心感谢中,全场时不时响起笑声和掌声。
诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)科研与知识交流副院长刘任远教授在最后提到,此时此地的相聚不该让大家因离别而难过,而应该为成长而欢笑,“本次项目不是结束,而是又一个开始,期望学员能够带着培训中点燃的火种,在未来继续为数字化运营和转型作出贡献。”
诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)高管培训项目致力于为行业领导者(如中国中车、航空工业、华润医药、中国电建等)提供持续的解决方案和智慧支持,培育创新能力,培养国际人才。项目以学院教授们丰富的行业实践与咨询经验为核心,与工科、人文社科等多学科课程紧密结合,将前沿学术知识、实践成果、全球最佳商业实践案例以及博雅教育理念传递到课堂。诺丁汉大学商学院(中国)高管培训项目与行业领军者联系紧密,积极探索大型企业的人才需求和管理战略,为中国企业走向世界及培养世界级的企业领导者贡献力量。

title: 招生专业
content:
本科专业
英语与应用语言学 文学学士(2+2/4年)
本专业旨在培养学生较高的英语交际、评论水平,深入了解西方语言学理论和应用语言学分析技能。与此同时,本专业特别注重培养学生深刻理解在特定语境中如何使用语言,分析语言如何受不同用途、不同环境和不同受众所影响。
课程结构
学生可选择四年都在宁波诺丁汉大学就读,也可选择后两年在英国诺丁汉大学就读。
英语语言文学 文学学士(2+2)
本专业立足于已在英国诺丁汉大学成功开设125年的课程基础之上,前两年的课程设置与英语与应用语言学专业相同,其后两年的课程旨在通过对英语语言文学的欣赏,帮助学生全面理解文学作品中英语语言的性质和用途
课程结构
学生的第一、第二年在宁波诺丁汉大学学习,第三、第四年则赴英国诺丁汉大学学习。
英语研究与国际商务 文学学士(4年)
本专业旨在结合语言学与国际商务的理论知识和两者在不同意识形态领域的实践,帮助学生较好地理解英语语言的本质,熟练运用语言,进行商务交流和企业管理。学生需要在教育与英语语言文学系修满240 学分,在商学院修满120 学分。本专业课程在教授语言的同时,还特别关注于国际商务问题,对商务管理的理论和实践做了综合、全面、充分的整合。
硕士专业
教育与英语语言文学系开设了以下授课型硕士专业:
应用语言学 文学硕士
国际高等教育 文学硕士
英语翻译 文学硕士
对外英语教学(TESOL)文学硕士
博士生项目
宁波诺丁汉大学的教育与英语语言文学系与英国诺丁汉大学的英语学院合作开办博士生项目。英国诺丁汉大学的英语学院是英国历史最悠久、最有声望的英语学院之一。

title: 就业与发展
content:

title: 本科专业
content:
本科专业介绍
国际传播系所开设的本科专业包含各式各样令人激动的主题,并且由来自于世界各地的师资团队教授。在这里,学生们能获得来自于学者们的最新研究成果及理念,这些学者们不仅在全球范围内发表文章,而且通过周游世界获悉来自于业内人士及同事之间的讨论与理论,同时也向他们展示了自己的研究成果。本科课程包括最新教学技术支持的讲座与研讨会,围绕如何沟通交流的发展性理论和展现在我们面前的重要的全球化趋势理论。所教授的课程使学生们了解到全新的理念,经验以及挑战,使之具备真正意思上的国际视野。
具体课程内容包括对传播理论、东欧和西欧社会,传媒研究,传播与社会的介绍,对文化研究、电影和选修课程的学习等等。伴随着这些具体的专业设置,同学们也会发现学校有一个非常现代化且资源丰富的图书馆,包括观看电影和DVD的视听中心,各种体育设施和社交活动,这些设施以及活动都旨在提高学生们的语言及沟通技巧。
国际传播学 文学学士
国际传播学专业通过研究不同形式的视觉和语言、新技术、政治、大众文化以及新闻媒体,来探索复杂的传播、媒体和文化世界。该专业为学生提供了范围极广的课程,包括数字媒体、移动传媒、大众传媒、数字人文、电影研究、游戏研究、传播理论及文化研究等。此外,学生将从初学者水平开始学习一门欧洲语言(法语、西班牙语或德语)或一门亚洲语言( 日语或韩语),直至达到高级水平,该语言课程将构成二至四年级的核心课程。
国际传播学专业于2007 年获批为浙江省“十二五”本科高校重点专业及优势专业项目,并入选2020年度省级一流本科专业建设点
。

title: 硕博专业
content:
授课型硕士介绍
国际传播系开设的硕士研究生专业以快速的发展态势成为备受赞誉的专业,所有课程都是由国际化的学者团队教授,本专业能满足那些希望把国际传播学与其专业知识相结合的任何其他学科毕业生的需要,它不仅为学生提供接触近代传播理论和方法论发展的机会,也让学生洞察当代媒体传播产业的知识和技术。
在研究生学习阶段,最重要的一个组成部分就是毕业论文的准备。学生们可以轻松找到有能力的和有知识的教师团队来协助完成这项重要的任务,并且确保完成具有高水准的毕业论文。
国际传播学 文学硕士
通过本专业的学习能让你从不同角度深入钻研传播学的理论及实践,你将深入研究一些具有批判性的理论概论,其中包括创意产业、文化、数字传媒、全球化、信息化社会、大众传媒和多元文化论与科技。你也能将你所学的知识应用到国际相关问题的分析中。
博士生项目
我们的博士课程能为学生提供跨越宁波诺丁汉大学和英国诺丁汉大学两个校区的灵活的指导和管理。宁波诺丁汉大学的博士研究生主要在本校学习,根据不同专业的实际需要也可到英国诺丁汉大学学习或开展学术研究。毕业生将被授予英国诺丁汉大学相应的博士学位,中国籍学生可在教育部留学服务中心进行学位认证。

title: 交换与留学
content:
交换与留学
国际传播系的本科生有机会在大三的时候到国外的其他学校去交换一个学期或者一年。对那些想感受一下其他国家的校园生活的学生们来说将会是非常可贵的经历及体验,通过交换生项目,学生们有机会提高他们的语言技能、学习他国的文化、选择不同的课程和项目进行学习,为他们以后向国外的院校申请研究生学位做好充分的准备。
除了可以交换到英国校区和马来西亚校区,国际传播系的学生如果满足相应的条件,还可以到很多合作院校进行交换。
